- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +10% above recent peak or use 3-period moving average.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) and price drops >5% from recent high, model underestimates; add 1–3% buffer to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias in early 30d horizon — if forecast is >10% above 18d average, adjust downward by 1–3% unless sentiment is strong bullish.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture short-term volatility; use 2-period EWMA or sentiment-weighted average for smoothing.
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to lagging sentiment shifts — if sentiment turns negative within 5 days, adjust forecast 3–5 days ahead by -1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
